picks.style: late antique lament, low bowed strings and sparse frame drum, weary baritone, slow, bitter, unresolved
picks.why: Alaric alone after the rout: 'I fear my friends more than my foes ... my life is a burden; why prolong it?' — the one human voice in the panegyric.

picks.style: roman civic invocation, cithara and low horns, commanding female voice, stately, reproachful, processional
picks.why: Rome herself speaking as a slighted mother, counting the white horses and the arch she built for a son who would not come.

picks.style: latin epic defiance, war horns and thunderous drums, roaring bass over massed voices, driving, blasphemous, building to a crack
picks.why: Capaneus shouting at Jupiter to come down and fight him, and Jove laughing — the most electric moment in the poem.

picks.style: dream-shadow lullaby, bowed vibraphone and soft harp, breathy low voice, very slow, drifting, narcotic
picks.why: The House of Sleep: dreams true and false clinging to the doorposts, lamps breathing out from their sinking flames.

picks.style: latin grief-lament, solo viola and skin drum, raw contralto, slow, keening, animal
picks.why: The tigress licking the warm rock where her cubs lay, watching herds walk past unhunted — grief made into a hunger with nothing to eat.

picks.style: nordic folk, bowed lyre and frame drum, low male chant, stark, cold, alliterative and measured
picks.why: 'We have heard of heroes in ages past, of twelve true thanes under the turning stars' — the opening does everything an opening should.

picks.style: old english winter chant, bowed lyre and bone flute, hoarse male voice, very slow, glacial, sparse
picks.why: Rime and frost as 'the hoar-frost warriors' locking the homeland, ice bridging the pale brine-road — pure Old English cold.

picks.style: grim mead-hall dirge, bowed lyre and deep drum, layered male voices, heavy, ironic, tolling
picks.why: The drowning told as a feast: 'a bitter beer-serving. The cup-bearers did not fail ... a drink ready at once.'

picks.style: hellenistic lyre song, solo kithara, clear tenor, gentle, elegiac, unhurried
picks.why: 'Your nightingales live on, and on them Hades ... shall never lay his hand' — the most quoted couplet in Greek epigram.

picks.style: greek call-and-response dirge, low aulos and hand drum, two alternating voices, spare, uncanny, dry
picks.why: The dialogue with the dead Charidas: 'And the ways up?' 'A lie.' 'And Pluto?' 'A tale.' — already written as call and response.

picks.style: greek doorstep serenade, plucked lyre and soft reed, wounded tenor, slow, insomniac, repeating
picks.why: 'So may you sleep, Conopion' — the sleepless lover on the cold porch, with a refrain and a curse for an ending.

picks.style: english thanksgiving hymn, acoustic guitar and chamber strings, warm female vocal, unhurried, grateful, building
picks.why: A litany of concrete blessings — hay, moonlight on the sea, the faithful eyes of dogs — that reads as one long grace.

picks.style: georgian dramatic air, harpsichord and cello, agitated soprano, insistent, questioning, quickening
picks.why: The heart interrogated at her own feet: a whole stanza of 'Why dost thou...' — anaphora already written for singing.

picks.style: comic drawing-room ballad, fortepiano and pizzicato strings, arch soprano, brisk, deadpan, quatrain-strophic
picks.why: The Pope refusing his pills: 'Whoever spoke — the Pope replied, Butter and Margravine.' A complete joke in singable quatrains.

picks.style: georgian reflective air, chamber organ and viola, grave tenor, slow, wistful, measured
picks.why: The echo that revives a dying note set against the life that cannot be revived — one clean image carrying the whole poem.

picks.style: english anapaestic compliment-song, baroque guitar and flute, light tenor, tripping, gallant, brisk
picks.why: 'The Plumb, and the Peach, with Apollo conspire' — a four-line compliment that dances in its own metre.

picks.style: roman street lampoon, reedy pipes and hand drum, sneering male voice, jaunty, mocking, quick
picks.why: Only candidate, but it carries a real forum-lampoon: the emperor who wanted to be Felix and refused to be Pius, and his worse reply.

picks.style: ancient greek lament, single lyre and low drone, solo male voice, very slow, hollow, sparse
picks.why: Two lines only, but they are the Homeric ones: the breath that leaves the lips and never comes back to wake the dead.
